key_insight: PolicyIK uses goal-conditioned reinforcement learning to translate a desired robot-hand position and orientation into arm-joint motion. It targets precise inverse kinematics, but the provided abstract is incomplete and includes no performance results.
problem_solved: Inverse kinematics is difficult because multiple joint configurations can produce the same pose, singularities complicate motion, controllers require manual tuning, and physical-robot training data are expensive.
method: Frame inverse kinematics as a goal-conditioned reinforcement learning task.
Use a learned policy to update arm joints toward a target end-effector pose.
Target high-precision pose control; training details and evaluation results are not available in the supplied excerpt.
impact: Reliable learned inverse kinematics could help vision-language-action policies execute precise arm movements and adapt across robot embodiments. The excerpt does not establish accuracy gains, transfer performance, or reduced tuning costs.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: target hand pose → PolicyIK → joint motion → resulting hand pose.
Robot-arm illustration showing different joint configurations reaching the same target.
Target-versus-achieved pose overlay highlighting position and orientation error.
Challenge icons for singularities, controller tuning, and costly physical-robot data.
paper_title: PolicyIK: High-Precision Inverse Kinematics for Robot Arms with Reinforcement Learning
paper_authors: Yuhan Liu, Xinqi Liu, Zixuan Dong, Keith W. Ross, Shenji Wan
